description: Comprehensive multi-criteria lunar landing site decision synthesis report.

profile_snapshot.name: 14-Day Long Duration Rover Profile
profile_snapshot.description: Tests scope mismatch handling when evaluated against 72h scenario

min_full_sunlight_hours.name: Minimum Full Sunlight Duration
min_full_sunlight_hours.description: Minimum cumulative duration where the solar disk is 100% unoccluded by terrain. Full sunlight is a geometric subset of total sunlight.
min_full_sunlight_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Requires 100% solar disk clearance above local horizon.

min_sunlight_percentage.name: Minimum Sunlight Percentage
min_sunlight_percentage.description: Ratio of total illuminated hours to total mission duration (expressed in %).
min_sunlight_percentage.scientific_disclaimer: Denominator is the total user-configured mission duration.

min_daily_sunlight_hours.name: Minimum Daily Sunlight Duration
min_daily_sunlight_hours.description: Minimum geometric illumination required per standard 24.0-hour Earth day interval (distinct from the ~708.7 h lunar synodic day). Evaluates cumulative hours with solar disk clearance f_disk > 0 in each standard 24h operational window.
min_daily_sunlight_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Applies per standard 24.0-hour Earth operational day. Partial illumination (f_disk > 0) contributes to geometric duration; does not evaluate solar incident cosine angle or battery charge efficiency.

min_total_earth_visible_hours.name: Minimum Total Geometric Earth Visibility
min_total_earth_visible_hours.description: Minimum cumulative duration of direct geometric line-of-sight to Earth across the mission analysis window.
min_total_earth_visible_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Geometric Earth visibility does not guarantee an operational radio link; RF link budget, antenna pointing, and data rates are not modeled.

max_continuous_earth_blackout_hours.name: Maximum Continuous Earth LOS Blackout
max_continuous_earth_blackout_hours.description: Maximum allowable duration of continuous Direct-to-Earth loss of signal (LOS).
max_continuous_earth_blackout_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Periods where Earth disk is completely obstructed by local terrain.

min_daily_earth_visible_hours.name: Minimum Daily Earth Visibility
min_daily_earth_visible_hours.description: Minimum Direct-to-Earth line-of-sight required per standard 24.0-hour Earth day interval (distinct from the ~708.7 h lunar synodic day). Evaluates cumulative visible contact hours in each standard 24h operational window.
min_daily_earth_visible_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Applies per standard 24.0-hour Earth day. Line-of-sight clearance does not evaluate RF link budget or ground station scheduling.

min_full_disk_earth_visible_hours.name: Minimum Full-Disk Earth Visibility
min_full_disk_earth_visible_hours.description: Cumulative duration where the entire Earth disk is completely unoccluded by terrain. Full-disk visibility is a geometric subset of total visibility.
min_full_disk_earth_visible_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Full-disk clearance without partial atmospheric limb clipping.

min_elevation_m.name: Minimum Surface Elevation
min_elevation_m.description: Minimum surface elevation above the IAU 1,737,400 m lunar sphere datum.
min_elevation_m.scientific_disclaimer: Reference datum is the IAU Moon 2000 Sphere (R = 1,737,400.0 m).

max_elevation_m.name: Maximum Surface Elevation
max_elevation_m.description: Maximum surface elevation above the IAU 1,737,400 m lunar sphere datum.
max_elevation_m.scientific_disclaimer: Reference datum is the IAU Moon 2000 Sphere (R = 1,737,400.0 m).

max_roughness_factor.name: Maximum Local Terrain Roughness Factor
max_roughness_factor.description: Local standard deviation of slope within the landing area footprint.
max_roughness_factor.scientific_disclaimer: Derived from local 5 m DEM neighborhood variance.

sections.title: Mission Cover & Executive Overview
sections.summary: LUNAVISTA comprehensive landing site navigation and mission decision support compilation for mission 'Artemis Polar Scout-1'. Evaluation conducted against mission profile '14-Day Long Duration Rover Profile' across 4 candidate lunar alternatives.

sections.title: Executive Summary & Trade-off Synopsis
sections.summary: Multi-criteria evaluation of 4 candidate alternatives for mission 'Artemis Polar Scout-1'. Of the candidate pool, 1 satisfied all evaluated hard constraints, 0 failed one or more hard constraints, and 1 possessed unverified/indeterminate requirements due to partial DEM coverage or missing assessment layers. The decision support engine highlights key trade-offs in solar illumination, continuous darkness periods, Earth line-of-sight visibility, and local topographic slope.

details.winner_declaration: No automated winner declared; decision authority reserved for mission planners.

callouts: High soft-preference scores do NOT compensate for hard constraint violations.
Official landing site certification requires independent geotechnical and engineering validation.

sections.title: Mission Profile & Requirements Definition
sections.summary: Requirements defined under profile '14-Day Long Duration Rover Profile' (Version 1). Mission architecture: Robotic Exploration. Nominal analysis duration: 14.0 Earth Days.

sections.title: Candidate Landing Sites & Geodetic Overview
sections.summary: Overview of 4 candidate landing sites in the lunar south polar circumpolar region. Referenced to IAU Moon 2000 Sphere / Lunar Mean Earth reference frame.

sections.title: Candidate Screening & Hard Constraint Matrix
sections.summary: Verification results for all active hard constraints. Every candidate must satisfy 100% of hard constraints.
callouts: Any single hard constraint failure strictly disqualifies an alternative from recommendation.

sections.title: Mission Window Planner & Celestial Temporal Analysis
sections.summary: Temporal simulation of solar illumination and direct Earth line-of-sight visibility computed using topocentric horizons and SPICE ephemerides.

sections.title: Terrain Suitability & Topographic Assessment
sections.summary: Topographic analysis derived from NASA LOLA 5m/pixel polar digital elevation model.
disclaimers: Official LOLA surface roughness dataset is not loaded; micro-roughness (<5m scale) remains unsupported.
Topographic slope alone does not guarantee rover traversability or landing gear touchdown stability.

sections.title: Terrain Horizon & Topocentric Celestial Geometry
sections.summary: Evaluation of 360° regional terrain horizon elevation profiles and celestial body elevation tracks. Finite solar disk integration resolves full, partial, and occulted illumination states.

details.ephemeris_source: NASA JPL DE421 / SPICE Planetary Ephemerides

sections.title: Multi-Criteria Mission Trade-off Analysis
sections.summary: Evaluation of candidate alternatives across user-configured preference dimensions. Normalization uses Min-Max reference bounds. Strict separation of hard constraints from soft preferences.
callouts: A composite preference score is a decision support metric, not a physical landing safety rating.

sections.title: Comprehensive Alternatives Comparison Matrix
sections.summary: Side-by-side technical comparison of candidate alternatives across all mission domains.

sections.title: Uncertainty, Data Limitations & Epistemic Boundaries
sections.summary: Transparent documentation of scientific and operational boundaries.
disclaimers: DEM resolution is limited to 5 meters per pixel; sub-pixel boulders and micro-craters are unresolved.
Surface roughness data is unavailable in the current raster catalogue and excluded from scoring.
Direct Earth line-of-sight indicates geometric visibility only; RF link budget must be independently verified.
Solar disk illumination does not compute solar array electrical power output or thermal equilibrium.
Topographic slope does not establish geotechnical bearing capacity or landing touchdown stability.

sections.title: Final Findings & Human Decision Authority Checklist
sections.summary: Final synthesis of mission candidate evaluations. The decision support system presents factual trade-offs, Pareto non-dominated alternatives, and constraint compliance. The final landing site selection requires explicit multi-disciplinary mission planner sign-off.
callouts: Automated Winner Recommendation: NONE (Human Decision Authority Reserved)

frozen_scenarios_data.name: Connecting Ridge — Crater Rim Crest
frozen_scenarios_data.description: High-elevation crest candidate along Connecting Ridge offering extensive line-of-sight visibility and prolonged solar illumination.

frozen_scenarios_data.name: Connecting Ridge — Candidate 01A
frozen_scenarios_data.description: Artemis candidate landing zone along the southern ridge saddle with moderate local slopes and extended sunlight windows.

frozen_scenarios_data.name: Connecting Ridge — South Rim Ridge
frozen_scenarios_data.description: Candidate outpost adjacent to the Shackleton crater outer flank overlooking the permanently shadowed interior.

frozen_scenarios_data.name: Connecting Ridge — North Saddle Outpost
frozen_scenarios_data.description: Northern approach shoulder candidate evaluated for rover transit accessibility and landing hazard safety.

scientific_disclaimers: A composite preference score is a user-configured decision aid, not a physical landing safety rating.
Pareto optimality indicates absence of strictly superior alternatives under selected dimensions, not absolute mission feasibility.
Hard constraint compliance does not establish lunar landing safety, geotechnical bearing capacity, or hazard absence.
Geometric Earth line-of-sight visibility does not establish an operational RF communications link budget.
Solar disk visibility does not calculate solar array electrical power output or thermal equilibrium.
Candidate alternatives must never be declared as universally best or safest.

human_decision_checklist.item: Review and approve all candidate hard-constraint evaluation results
Verify direct Earth RF communications link margin under local terrain horizon
Assess lander touchdown stability under local slope and boulder distribution
Verify battery state-of-charge margin for maximum continuous darkness intervals
Concurrence by Mission Operations Directorate on final landing site selection

min_total_earth_visible_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Does not model RF ground station elevation masks or Deep Space Network scheduling.

max_continuous_earth_blackout_hours.name: Maximum Continuous Earth LOS Blackout
max_continuous_earth_blackout_hours.description: Desirable threshold for maximum autonomous rover drive between ground contacts.
max_continuous_earth_blackout_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Continuous periods where terrain completely obstructs Earth disk.

min_daily_earth_visible_hours.name: Minimum Daily Earth Visibility
min_daily_earth_visible_hours.description: Minimum Direct-to-Earth line-of-sight required per standard 24.0-hour Earth day interval (distinct from the ~708.7 h lunar synodic day). Evaluates cumulative visible contact hours in each standard 24h operational window.
min_daily_earth_visible_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Applies per standard 24.0-hour Earth day. Line-of-sight clearance does not evaluate RF link budget or ground station scheduling.

min_full_disk_earth_visible_hours.scientific_disclaimer: Full-disk clearance without partial atmospheric limb clipping.

max_local_slope_deg.description: Maximum wheel slip / tip-over grade limit for robotic rover traverse.
max_local_slope_deg.scientific_disclaimer: Derived from LOLA 5 m DEM slopes. Does not model rock hazards smaller than DEM pixel.
